name: Recognise what a sequence counts by
description: Student can recognise a skip counting sequence and say whether it is counting by twos, fives or tens.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 5, 10, 15, 20, the student says it is counting by fives.
commonError: Student sees the numbers as separate facts and does not notice the constant jump.
checkpointTask: Show three sequences (by 2s, 5s, 10s). Ask the student what each is counting by.

name: Continue a skip counting sequence
description: Student can continue a skip counting sequence forwards by twos, fives or tens.
commonError: Student adds one each time instead of the skip size, or loses the count past a tens boundary.
checkpointTask: Give the start of three skip counts. Ask the student to say the next three numbers in each.

name: Find a missing number in a skip count
description: Student can find a missing number in a skip counting sequence.
commonError: Student copies a neighbouring number, or counts by ones to fill the gap and miscounts.
checkpointTask: Pose three skip counts each with one gap. Ask the student to find the missing number.

name: Create a skip counting pattern with objects
description: Student can create a skip counting pattern using objects, shapes or symbols.
exampleOfSuccess: The student lays out groups of five counters and labels them 5, 10, 15, 20.
commonError: Student makes groups of unequal size, so the count does not skip evenly.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to build a counting-by-fives pattern with counters and label the totals.

name: Describe the rule of a skip counting pattern
description: Student can describe the rule in a skip counting sequence, such as how much it goes up by each time.
exampleOfSuccess: Looking at 2, 4, 6, 8, the student says it goes up by two each time.
commonError: Student describes the numbers but not the constant change between them.
checkpointTask: Show a skip counting sequence. Ask the student to explain the rule for getting the next number.

name: Continue a growing pattern made by skip counting
description: Student can continue a growing pattern where each step adds the same amount, using objects or shapes.
exampleOfSuccess: Given towers of 2, 4, 6 blocks, the student builds the next tower with 8 blocks.
commonError: Student repeats the last tower instead of adding the next step, or adds a different amount.
checkpointTask: Show a growing block pattern (2, 4, 6). Ask the student to build the next one or two steps.
reviewNotes: From elaboration 2. Bridges skip counting to growing patterns, the late rung.

name: Recognise a repeating pattern
description: Student can recognise when a sequence is a repeating pattern.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown red, blue, red, blue, red, blue, the student says it is a repeating pattern.
commonError: Student calls any sequence a pattern, including ones with no repeat.
checkpointTask: Show two sequences, one repeating and one not. Ask which is a repeating pattern.

name: Continue a repeating pattern
description: Student can continue a repeating pattern with objects, shapes, symbols or numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: Given circle, square, circle, square, the student continues circle, square.
commonError: Student adds elements that do not follow the repeat, or stops the pattern partway through a unit.
checkpointTask: Give three repeating patterns. Ask the student to add the next two elements to each.

name: Identify the repeating unit
description: Student can identify the part that repeats (the unit of repeat) in a pattern.
exampleOfSuccess: For red, blue, green, red, blue, green, the student says the repeating part is red, blue, green.
commonError: Student names a single element as the unit, or includes part of a second repeat in the unit.
checkpointTask: Show three repeating patterns. Ask the student to point out the part that keeps repeating in each.
reviewNotes: Core to the descriptor and Y1-AS-10 ('identifying the repeating unit').

name: Create a repeating pattern
description: Student can create their own repeating pattern with objects, shapes or symbols.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a clap, clap, stamp pattern and repeats it three times.
commonError: Student makes a sequence with no clear repeat, or changes the unit partway.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to make a repeating pattern with counters or actions and repeat it at least three times.

name: Find the missing part in a repeating pattern
description: Student can find and fill a missing element in a repeating pattern.
exampleOfSuccess: Given triangle, circle, triangle, __, triangle, circle, the student says circle.
commonError: Student fills the gap with the wrong element by copying a neighbour rather than using the repeat.
checkpointTask: Pose repeating patterns each with one element hidden. Ask the student what is missing.

name: Make the same pattern with different materials
description: Student can copy the structure of a repeating pattern using different materials.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown red, red, blue, the student makes the same structure with claps as clap, clap, stamp.
commonError: Student copies the materials rather than the structure, or changes the repeat when swapping materials.
checkpointTask: Show a repeating pattern. Ask the student to make the same pattern using different objects or actions.
reviewNotes: Late rung: recognising pattern structure as separable from the specific materials.
